hidden_case.analysis: The compiler accepts a cyclic SUPERSEDE chain. This does not violate the specific acceptance wording ('refuses a decision that orphans its predecessor') because every predecessor in the cycle does resolve; it is a scope limitation (no cycle detection), not an orphan-refusal failure. Note: the sibling unit po03-wa-b2e7-038-lineage-preservation DOES detect exactly this cycle case (verified independently, see its review), so the two-unit system together covers this gap even though 033 alone does not.

additional_findings: Committed __pycache__/disposition_compiler.cpython-312.pyc bytecode was listed as manifest artifact-001 at the original result commit 402c277618bcf4ba659588381f11b8fadf4e7424, despite a .gitignore in the same directory excluding '__pycache__/' and '*.py[cod]'. This was later cleaned up in the branch's final commit d35c88959f3c16bfbd85d8fe87e5f373ebe210ea ('remove bytecode and exercise pinned pack detector'), which removed the pyc file across all 8 c5 units. The manifest.json at the branch tip still references the older commit and still lists the pyc as an artifact; this is a stale-but-not-false record since the referenced historical commit object is immutable and still readable by hash. Not disqualifying, but sloppy for a 'portable-runtime' commission where committing version-specific bytecode is counter to the stated goal.

vacuous_test_check.method: Manually traced what a trivial stub (identity/no-op validation) would do against each of the 4 tests; 3 of 4 tests assert DispositionError is raised on invalid input, which a trivial stub would not raise. Tests are not vacuous.
